itinerary.cal: Best climbed June-Sept once the Chilliwack River ford, the Impasse and the Challenger Glacier are in reasonable shape; the Ross Lake Resort water taxi (used for the Beaver Pass variant) requires advance reservations.

days.note: From the Hannegan Pass trailhead climb about 2,000 ft in 4 miles to Hannegan Pass, drop past Boundary Camp into the Chilliwack valley, and leave the trail where the faint, unsigned climbers' path for Easy Ridge fords the Chilliwack (log crossings here are unreliable). Climb steeply onto Easy Ridge and camp near the tarns on its crest. A long day with a loaded pack: about 8 hours on foot is typical.
days.title: Hannegan Pass and the Chilliwack to Easy Ridge
days.objective: Camp on the crest of Easy Ridge

days.note: Follow the faint path along the crest over Easy Peak, which has more tent sites and a tarn, to the notch called the Impasse. Where the direct crossing is unsafe, drop off the crest around it and re-climb an exposed class 4 step beyond, then cross the snowfields to Perfect Pass. In fog, keep away from Whatcom Peak's summit wall, which steepens where the pass levels into a saddle.
days.title: Easy Ridge over the Impasse to Perfect Pass
days.objective: Camp at Perfect Pass (about 6,300 ft)

days.note: Get down from Perfect Pass onto the Challenger Glacier (depending on melt-out, about 200 ft of wet class 4 downclimbing and sometimes a short rappel across a moat), rope up, cross the bergschrund and climb steepening snow to the summit rocks, watching for the moat below them. A class 3 scramble leads to the 50 ft, 5.5-5.7 summit pitch; rappel it once and reverse the glacier to Perfect Pass. Some parties pack up the same afternoon and recross the Impasse to shorten the walk out.
days.title: Summit day via the Challenger Glacier
days.objective: Climb Mount Challenger via the Challenger Glacier and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the approach: back along Easy Ridge, down to the Chilliwack ford, and up the long climb to Hannegan Pass before the easy descent to the car.
days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike back out to the Hannegan Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip via Easy Ridge (add a spare day for weather), with camps on Easy Ridge and at Perfect Pass and one glacier summit day from Perfect Pass.

sectionBreakdown.note: From the Hannegan Pass trailhead climb to Hannegan Pass, drop into the Chilliwack valley, ford the river and climb steeply onto Easy Ridge to camp. The second day follows the crest over Easy Peak and around the Impasse to camp at Perfect Pass.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Approach over Easy Ridge to the Perfect Pass camp

sectionBreakdown.note: An early start down from Perfect Pass onto the Challenger Glacier, roped across the bergschrund and up steepening snow to the summit rocks, then a class 3 scramble and a short 5.5-5.7 pitch to the top.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Perfect Pass up the Challenger Glacier to the summit

sectionBreakdown.note: Rappel the summit pitch and reverse the glacier to Perfect Pass, then pack up and retrace Easy Ridge, the Chilliwack ford and the long climb back over Hannegan Pass to the car. Many parties keep a spare day for weather.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Back to Perfect Pass, then Easy Ridge and out to the trailhead

timing.recommendedStart: Early morning (before 6 AM) for multiday climbs to maximize daylight

days.note: Hike Lake Serene trail (4.1 miles, 2000 ft gain, 2-2.5 hours), approach cirque (30 min), scout wall and bivy location (1-2 hours).
days.title: Day 1

days.note: 5: Climbing days with portaledge camps. First ascensionists climbed Pitches 1-3 with bivy on Pitch 3. Pitch 4 (crux A3+) and Pitch 8 (Fang Roof) are highlights. Days 6-7: Finish upper pitches to summit, then full rappel descent (10-12 hours). Multiday success requires disciplined pacing and weather monitoring.
days.title: Day 2

timing.recommendedStart: Early morning (before 6 AM) for multiday climbs to maximize daylight

days.note: Hike the Lake Serene trail, about 4 miles and 2,000 ft in 2-2.5 hours, cross to the cirque below the wall in about half an hour, then scout the line and the bivy site.
days.title: Lake Serene to the base of the wall
days.objective: Bivy below the wall

days.note: Climb the lower pitches and set up the portaledge; the first ascent party slept on pitch 3.
days.title: Lower wall
days.objective: Portaledge camp on the lower wall

days.note: Climb through the hard aid of the crux pitch and the roof higher up, then finish the upper pitches to the top.
days.title: Upper wall to the summit
days.objective: Reach the summit

days.note: Rappel the full route, most of the day with haul bags, then walk back down the Lake Serene trail.
days.title: Rappel and hike out
days.objective: Back to the Lake Serene trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: About four days for a repeat party: a day to the base, two days on the wall and a day to rappel and walk out. The first ascent took seven.
